reviewedFrom: Month-end close controls: a closed period accepts no postings; a source dated into a closed period must surface as blocked (never silently re-dated or dropped) and block later closes until cured by reopening; manual journals need an independent reviewer before close; a failed close leaves the period open and a retry produces exactly the books a clean close would; each close's saved statements report that period's balances. POC figures follow docs/books-revenue-recognition.md §5 (July of the worked example). Pending licensed-CPA review (B16.3). Amounts are integer cents.

late-source-into-closed-period.derivation: July closes with 1,000 billed. A 500 invoice dated July 25 arrives after the close: it must show as blocked, leave July's ledger unchanged and block the August close. Reopening July posts it on its own date; reclosing July produces a new digest; August then closes. A direct journal into closed July is refused.

unreviewed-journal-proposal-blocks-close.derivation: A manual journal proposed by the accountant blocks close until a different person reviews it; the proposer cannot approve their own proposal.

close-failure-resumes.derivation: A close that fails after recognition — at the statement snapshot, or at the final lock after snapshots are saved — must leave the period open with no close digest; a retry must finish with the clean-close ledger (worked example July), exactly one recognition entry and one saved statement per type.

twelve-month-sequence-snapshots.derivation: One 1,000 invoice per month, each month closed in order: twelve distinct close digests, and each month's saved balance sheet reports receivables of 1,000 x month number.

quarter-end.derivation: Service invoices of 1,000, 2,000 and 3,000 in July, August and September, each month closed in order. Each month reads as closed from its saved statements. A quarter has no saved statement of its own: it is computed from the ledger (never labelled closed) and equals the three closed months together, 6,000.00; September's saved balance sheet carries 6,000.00 of receivables. Reopening September then August (newest first) for a late August invoice; the 500.00 invoice dated August 28 posts, August and September reclose, and the quarter reads 6,500.00 with 6,500.00 receivable saved at September 30.

all-supported-modules.derivation: The INTERCO-01 group's August (advance, repayment, the land company's bill and payroll summary paid by the builder, a shared insurance allocation) plus a 10,000.00 progress invoice collected August 12, a 36,000.00 truck bought for cash and depreciated 1,000.00, and a 100,000.00 loan drawn and paid 2,500.00 (2,000 principal, 500 interest). The WIP is prepared and independently reviewed, the 10,000.00 receipt in transit is supported, and the land company's statement (+500.00, -300.00) is matched and reconciled to 200.00. The checklist has no blocking failure, August closes, every ledger control passes, the close saves 8 consolidated and 6 per-company statements, and each company balances alone.

abandoned-close-resumes.derivation: A close dies right after freezing July (simulated by freezing without finishing). While frozen, operational postings into July are refused and a second close within 30 minutes refuses as already running. Once the freeze is older than 30 minutes, the next close resumes it and finishes with the clean worked-example July ledger and one recognition entry.

gate-matrix.derivation: A valid company closes with no blocking checks. Each invalid fixture — made through the product where one exists — fails exactly its own check, and its cure clears it. With two problems at once, curing one leaves the other failing (corrections never hide other open issues).

direct-job-cost-journal: GL job cost ties to the job-cost subledger
unreviewed-wip: WIP and POC reviewed through period end
invoice-not-yet-posted: Accounts receivable ties to the AR subledger

reviewer-cannot-mutate-gates.derivation: A read-only books reviewer (org_books_reviewer: books.read only) is refused, server-side, when running the close checks, supporting clearing balances, closing or reopening.
